description.value: To evaluate the cause of diagnostic errors in the visual interpretation of FDG-PET scans in patients with frontotemporal lobar degeneration and Alzheimer's disease, focusing on regional hypometabolism and diagnostic interpretation unanimity.

spans.text: To evaluate the cause of diagnostic errors in the visual interpretation of positron emission tomography scans with 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose (FDG-PET) in patients with frontotemporal lobar degeneration (FTLD) and Alzheimer's disease (AD).

description.value: Twelve trained raters independently reviewed FDG-PET scans while blinded to clinical and autopsy information; patients had pathologically confirmed FTLD or AD diagnoses.

spans.text: Twelve trained raters unaware of clinical and autopsy information independently reviewed FDG-PET scans and provided their diagnostic impression and confidence of either FTLD or AD.
Each rated the scans independently, without knowledge of the opinions of the others and blinded to any clinical data.

name.value: Association of regional hypometabolism with pathological diagnosis

definition.value: Associations between regional hypometabolism and a pathologically verified diagnosis of AD or FTLD.

spans.text: Associations between regional hypometabolism and a pathologically verified diagnosis of AD or FTLD were evaluated using a Chi-square test with Yates correction.

value: Hypometabolism in the anterior cingulate and anterior temporal cortices had higher specificities and higher likelihood ratios for a diagnosis of FTLD than hypometabolism in the temporoparietal cortex had for AD.
Ultimately, interpretation of an FDG-PET scan to distinguish between AD and FTLD cannot be based on the presence or absence of hypometabolism in a single region.

definition.value: Associations between regional hypometabolism and lack of unanimity among the raters for their overall interpretation.

spans.text: For the pathologically verified FTLD cases, associations between regional hypometabolism and lack of unanimity among the raters for their overall interpretation were evaluated with the Fisher's Exact test.

value: Temporoparietal hypometabolism was significantly associated with non-unanimous interpretations, occurring in 6/7 non-unanimous scans and in only 1/7 unanimously decided scans.
